title: The Marvel Role Rachel McAdams Turned Down
summary:
As Tony Stark's assistant and eventual wife Pepper Potts, Gwyneth Paltrow is one of the longest-lasting Marvel actors. She played Pepper from the very first Marvel movie, 2008's "Iron Man," to 2019's "Avengers: Endgame." But Paltrow was not the filmmakers' original first choice for the role.

In December 2006, Marvel Studios sent the "Iron Man" script exclusively to Rachel McAdams, hoping to cast her as Pepper. McAdams was on the rise, having broken out in 2004 by playing Regina George in "Mean Girls" and Allie Hamilton in "The Notebook," then starring in the hit airplane thriller "Red Eye" the following year. With "Iron Man" far from a guaranteed hit back then, hiring a rising star made sense. But she declined, which opened the door for Paltrow.

Speaking to Bustle in 2023, McAdams said "Iron Man" was just one of several blockbusters she turned down in that period, including "Casino Royale," "Mission: Impossible III" and "The Devil Wears Prada." She had been swept up into movie stardom and wanted time for herself. "I knew I was in such a lucky spot, but I also knew it wasn't quite jiving with my personality and what I needed to stay sane," she said.

McAdams took a break from acting between 2006 and 2008, appearing in only two films in that stretch. The break hardly hurt her career: she went on to earn a Best Supporting Actress Oscar nomination for "Spotlight." Amusingly, the first blockbuster she accepted after her break was the 2009 movie "Sherlock Holmes," starring Robert Downey Jr., who had just become a huge star as Iron Man. McAdams played Irene Adler, a thief and Holmes's love interest, and the two had plenty of chemistry on screen.

Marvel did not forget her number. McAdams eventually joined the Marvel universe as Dr. Christine Palmer in "Doctor Strange," returning for the sequel, "Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness." Director Sam Raimi later cast her in his survival thriller comedy "Send Help," in which she plays an overlooked office worker stuck on a desert island with her boss.
why_it_matters: This story shows that even big movie stars sometimes say no to huge roles, and that taking a break can be the right choice. McAdams still ended up joining Marvel years later.

background_read: Marvel movies are a long series of superhero films that share the same characters and stories.
Pepper Potts is the assistant and later wife of Tony Stark, the hero known as Iron Man.
Actors are sometimes offered big roles and choose to say no, for example to take a break or to try different kinds of films.
A break from acting does not always end a career: many actors return to even bigger roles afterwards.
